raw_response:
I am 73 this year. My wife and I still work these 4.1 mu ourselves — our son lives in town and only comes back for busy days. My back is not what it was, so I cannot farm like a young man. I have been on this soil 50 years, and I know what it gives.

This year I will plant about 2 mu of cotton on my best piece — the one near the well. Cotton is what brings cash in our village. Most neighbors still grow it, and the buyer from the county comes each autumn. I will plant 1.1 mu of mungbean after the cotton rows and on the edge strip — mungbean does not need much, and it puts something back in the soil. The other 1 mu I keep for millet, for our own eating and for the chickens. Selling millet is not worth much but we need grain at home.

For cotton I will buy improved seed from the dealer in the township — the Bt kind, because the bollworm used to ruin us before this seed. I will use about one bag (40 kg) of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu as base, then top-dress with about 15 kg urea per mu at flowering. That comes to around 18 kg nitrogen per mu. I know some say this is more than needed, but I would rather spend a little extra than see empty bolls. I will irrigate maybe 3 times — once before planting, once at flowering, once at boll-filling. Pesticide I still spray 5 or 6 times for aphids and mirid bugs even with Bt seed. I plough with the tractor service from the village — 40 yuan per mu, not bad.

For millet I use my own saved seed, the one my neighbor gave me years ago — it grows well here and does not need much. Half a bag of compound per mu, maybe 5 kg urea at jointing. One irrigation if the rain fails. Spray once for armyworm if I see them. I use rotary tiller, small plot.

For mungbean I put very little fertilizer — just a bit of phosphate at sowing, maybe 3 kg per mu of DAP. Mungbean makes its own nitrogen, everyone knows this. No irrigation usually unless very dry. One pesticide spray for pod borer. I plant by hand after cotton is up.

I am careful with money — pension is small, and fertilizer price went up again this spring. But cotton I will not cut corners on; that is where the income is.
